episodes.title: Who chooses the next search?
episodes.subtitle: The control arrangement is different from the retrieval machinery.

scenes.title: The query changed. Who chose the next action?
narration: A system searches, reads its top results, builds a different query, and searches again. A model may help choose the words. Is this agentic search? Pause and ask a more precise question: who decided that another search would happen?

Two pass pseudo relevance feedback can follow exactly that prescribed sequence every time. Its query contents adapt to the first ranking while its next action stays fixed. Result dependent content does not, by itself, establish agentic control.

scenes.title: Fixed, adaptive and agentic name different controls
narration: A fixed workflow follows a prescribed sequence. An adaptive workflow selects among branches explicitly enumerated by its designer. A rule, classifier or model may choose that branch. Using a model for the choice does not settle the category.

Agentic search lets a model plan at least part of a multi action retrieval trajectory from the task and its observations. Its tools are predefined too. The distinction is whether it assembles a sequence, rather than only selecting enumerated branches.

scenes.title: The brief specifies the task; the harness bounds the actions
narration: The task brief supplies scope, criteria, sources, coverage, stopping conditions and the required record. The harness defines available operations, reachable sources, budgets and limits. A tool means a callable operation, such as searching or fetching references, rather than an entire licensed product.
The model works within those permissions. Further reasoning cannot supply an unavailable operation or inaccessible source.

scenes.title: A long report does not establish agency
narration: Output format is a separate property. A scripted deep search can return records after repeated retrieval. An agentic search can also return records. Either fixed or model planned retrieval can precede a generated report or answer.

Length, fluency and citations show generation, not who controlled the search. Basic RAG retrieves then generates. Agentic RAG lets a model choose retrieval actions towards a generated response; agentic search is broader and need not generate prose.

scenes.title: Control does not replace the retriever’s scoring rule
narration: Hybrid describes contributing retrieval routes. Multi stage describes how operations follow earlier outputs. Agentic describes who chose the sequence. These properties can combine, but none automatically establishes the others.

Model planned repeated BM twenty five searches can be agentic without being hybrid. Fixed lexical and dense retrieval followed by fusion can be hybrid and multi stage without being agentic. The controller changes which operations run; it does not change BM twenty five’s scoring formula.

scenes.title: Assess the mode, not the brand
narration: The chapter’s April twenty twenty six account places Asta Find Paper in a semi rigid, predefined flow shaped by model decisions. It contrasts Undermind’s original deep search with Projects, which the account describes as dynamically selecting and chaining tools.

These are dated reference points along a continuum, not new product tests. One vendor can offer different control arrangements in different modes. Iteration or a model inside a pipeline is insufficient evidence of an independently planned trajectory.

scenes.title: A marketing label and a documented mechanism can differ
narration: An April twenty twenty six Web of Science Research Assistant post used fully agentic while describing automatic choice among task routes. That description is compatible with adaptive control; the post does not settle whether novel sequences can be composed.

It also documents user review and approval of a proposed strategy before retrieval, followed by an Advanced Search expression. That approval gate is a concrete control property. It is different from deciding when an ongoing search has enough evidence to stop.

scenes.title: Choose control for the procedure the task requires
narration: For a known task with a sound established procedure, fixed or adaptive control may be the better bargain. Agentic control can attempt an unanticipated sequence using available actions, with added cost, latency and variation between runs.
Inspect the required sequence, available actions and evidence of who chose the next move. The next film examines why more iterations can preserve a blind spot just as easily as repair one.

episodes.title: The blind spot that survives the loop
episodes.subtitle: More rounds do not automatically establish better coverage.

scenes.title: A simple request can require an unfamiliar sequence
narration: Find related papers that an article could have cited but did not. The chapter’s probe requires identifying the article, extracting its references, finding related work, and comparing identities. Would running more searches alone complete that task? Pause and identify the missing operation.

The comparison must actually happen. Our invented set diagram removes already cited identities from a related candidate pool. The remaining records are candidates for checking, not verified citation omissions; timing, relevance and metadata still need assessment.

scenes.title: A task probe is different from a product league table
narration: The author’s December twenty twenty five probe reports Asta stopping at the target lookup, and Consensus returning already cited papers despite four sub agents. SciSpace attempted reference extraction and comparison; most suggestions were uncited, but metadata caused some matching failures and completion was unclear.

General assistants also depended on access to the full text. This was one task type, not a general capability ranking. Passing or failing it does not establish robust agency across tasks or identify a failure’s sole cause.

scenes.title: The path taken does not reveal the available menu
narration: A trace records what the system did. It does not reveal every action it could have taken. Missing reference extraction or source access can block the task.
MCP can expose search operations to a controller: their inputs, outputs and purpose. Scite and Wiley AI Gateway provide examples in the chapter. The underlying retrieval algorithm stays separate.

scenes.title: An exposed service still has a defined boundary
narration: Wiley’s documented server returns relevant full text chunks with paper metadata. Scite documents tools and Search API filters, but does not document ranking parity with its web interface; its Assistant is not offered through MCP.

The controller chooses when to call those operations, what to ask and whether to search again. The exposed operations, authentication and library entitlements still apply. An endpoint does not provide every interface feature or a route around a subscription.

scenes.title: Earlier results can steer every later round
narration: The chapter illustrates a hypothetical search about open access and citations. Round one returns papers about overall citation differences, while selection bias methods are missing. Later searches follow the returned terminology and references, reinforcing the same aspect.

After three rounds the budget ends, with selection bias methods still unexplored. These are hypothetical recorded actions and observations, not private model reasoning. The example shows how a shortlist bottleneck can recur and influence the next search.

scenes.title: An alternative action can admit new candidates
narration: An alternative second action explicitly searches for open access, citation advantage and selection bias methods. Suppose that action retrieves methodological papers absent from the first round. The cumulative candidate pool can then expand, informing later choices.

The task brief, a librarian or the controller could prompt that action. It is not guaranteed to occur or succeed. Citation searching does not always stay inside one aspect; the illustration contrasts possible trajectories, not universal outcomes.

scenes.title: Stopping is a decision about unseen evidence
narration: A workflow may stop because its steps ended. A harness may impose a round limit or budget, or the user may interrupt. A model may instead decide that the evidence it has seen is sufficient.

That last decision applies a relevance criterion to results the user may not have inspected. Record it. A budget reached, declining yield or a model saying enough does not prove completeness, and two runs may stop differently.

scenes.title: Record actions, observations, options and stopping
narration: Evaluating the loop requires the available action menu as well as the executed trace, intermediate results and stopping conditions. Otherwise an access limit can look like reasoning failure, and an early omission can disappear behind a fluent final answer.

More rounds add latency and tokens. A known procedure may be cheaper and more reproducible when prescribed in advance. Choose the arrangement for the task, and evaluate what it recovered and what it failed to explore.

episodes.title: When zero results become a clue
episodes.subtitle: A failed query can inform another action without changing the index.

scenes.title: Nothing came back. Is the search over?
narration: A student wants a database for autism research. A catalogue search returns nothing. Should the system conclude that the library has nothing useful, or treat the failure as information for another attempt? Pause and consider what a database record is likely to say.

The chapter’s loop broadens to related subject areas and recovers useful database names. The request was for a database about a subject, not necessarily a database named after that subject. Recovery changes how the search is used.

scenes.title: Selected old queries met newer models
narration: The author’s June twenty twenty six demonstration replayed selected database queries from twenty twenty three zero result logs against the library’s Primo index, through a model and an MCP server. The request asked for a database for each topic.

The examples were selected rather than sampled, and newer models answered older queries. Read the account as exploratory failure recovery, not a success rate, a controlled benchmark, or a comparison proving superiority over human searchers.

scenes.title: A good synonym expansion can still miss the problem
narration: The comparison used Primo’s single pass Natural Language Search over the same index. For autism it produced a plausible OR expression including autistic disorder, ASD, autism spectrum, neurodevelopmental disorder and pervasive developmental disorder. It still returned zero results.

The source’s six terms stayed at the autism concept. The single pass rewrite did not use the zero result response to revise the query. More synonyms were not the same operation as choosing a broader subject area.

scenes.title: Move from a subject name to a database’s coverage
narration: The loop broadened autism into psychology, medicine, education and disability. In the selected example it returned PsycINFO, Education Research Complete and SocINDEX. Those names are reported outcomes from the chapter, not searches conducted for this video.
The keyword oriented endpoint did not need a new scoring formula for that sequence to become useful. The controller reformulated the request and tried again.

scenes.title: Broader concepts and newer knowledge both matter
narration: Other selected examples turned cost of living into inflation, household expenditure and consumer prices. Rolex watches became a question about luxury goods, producing Statista and Passport. The typo statis resolved to Statista.

The refinituv example reached LSEG, but that illustrates the dating problem: the recovered rebrand postdated the original query. A newer model knows things an older model might not. Do not attribute every improvement to the loop alone.

scenes.title: Several comparisons narrow the explanation
narration: The chapter reports that a holdings CSV also worked for the selected examples, and a smaller model made little difference there. That does not establish that model capability is generally irrelevant, or that MCP itself caused recovery.

The examples support feedback, broadening and another attempt, while changing other parts of the setup too. They do not isolate the loop as the sole cause. Fixed or adaptive workflows could also implement useful retries; better retrieval still matters.

scenes.title: The library knows facts the open web cannot supply
narration: The model can draw on public knowledge about familiar databases and subject areas. A little known or newly licensed database may receive less help. Current coverage, field quirks, embargo dates and this institution’s actual entitlements are local facts it cannot safely infer.

Those facts need authoritative library information. Recovery does not remove that work; it changes where it belongs. A specialised request about particular variables, companies and years can still exceed the available knowledge or tools.

scenes.title: Evaluate recovery as a property of the whole process
narration: A zero result can become an observation that informs the next action, while the retriever’s scoring function stays unchanged. In these selected examples, that helped recover useful results. It does not show that every retry succeeds or requires agentic control.

Record the failed query, the new action, what came back and why the search stopped. Choose control for the actual task and supply current local knowledge. The completed pipeline now lets us ask a diagnostic question: where did a particular search go wrong?
